dir="auto">Bug</h1>
<p dir="auto"><strong>- What is the current behavior?</strong></p>
<p dir="auto">I ran <code class="notranslate">netlify --telemetry-disable</code> on a fresh install (<code class="notranslate">rm -rf ~/.netlify</code>) and it connected to <code class="notranslate">cli.netlify.com</code>:</p>
<p dir="auto"><a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow" href="https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/408977/76146078-c5c0a200-6044-11ea-9710-4ebb7618afe4.png"><img width="1568" alt="Screen Shot 2020-03-07 at 07 24 56" src="https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/408977/76146078-c5c0a200-6044-11ea-9710-4ebb7618afe4.png" style="max-width: 100%;"></a></p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>- If the current behavior is a bug, please provide the steps to reproduce.</strong></p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>install netlify cli via yarn/npm</li>
<li>run <code class="notranslate">netlify --telemetry-disable</code></li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto"><strong>- What is the expected behavior?</strong></p>
<p dir="auto">Expected: I'm not spied on.</p>
<p dir="auto">Actual: Your app violates my consent.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>- Local Environment Information</strong></p>

<h1 dir="auto">Dear Netlify</h1>
<p dir="auto">Dear Netlify:</p>
<p dir="auto">I use and really like your service.  I was happy to hear you guys raised some money recently.  I was deeply disappointed to see that you have telemetry enabled in your app; I disabled it on all my systems using it but apparently it's still spying on me.</p>
<p dir="auto">This sort of spying is deeply unethical.  You are not entitled to silently spy on your users simply because they didn't realize that your app is spyware.  You are not entitled to <em>assume</em> consent just because you mentioned on your webpage that your apps will silently spy on your users.  This makes your app <strong>malware</strong>.</p>
<p dir="auto">"We're going to silently spy on you unless you read our whole website, notice that it's a spyware app, and then disable the spyware part" is not an ethical business practice.  You must <strong>OBTAIN CONSENT</strong> from your users to use their personal data.  You may not <em>assume consent</em>.</p>
<p dir="auto">What you're doing now is unethical and abusive.  That’s simply not affirmative consent. Imagine if you tried that in life! “Anyone who stays in this room after 5pm is consenting to be groped! Proceed at your own risk.”  Don't be that creep.  Please don't ship spyware.</p>
<p dir="auto">Note that fixing only this bug (the issue of sending telemetry when the user explicitly opts out) is not a complete solution.  You must <strong>stop spying on your users</strong> unless they have <em>explicitly agreed</em> to permit you to their usage information.</p>
<p dir="auto">Best,<br>
-<a class="user-mention notranslate" data-hovercard-type="user" data-hovercard-url="/users/sneak/hovercard" data-octo-click="hovercard-link-click" data-octo-dimensions="link_type:self" href="https://github.com/sneak">@sneak</a></p>
<p dir="auto">PS: "everyone else is doing it" is <em>not</em> an acceptable excuse for unethical behavior.</p>
<p dir="auto">PPS: "but the collection is anonymous!" is not an excuse either: transmitting a user's IP to your telemetry server leaks that user's location, which is a violation of their privacy.  IPs uniquely identify many, many users, and SNI is not yet encrypted.</p></div></div><div class="IssueBodyTaskList__-FlQre"><div role="toolbar" aria-label="Reactions" class="d-flex gap-1 <p dir="auto">It's <em>another thing entirely</em> to actively receive a revocation of consent, and then <em>proceed to send a telemetry event in direct violation of that</em>.</p>
<p dir="auto">Please don't spy on your users.</p></div></div><div role="toolbar" aria-label="Reactions" class="d-flex gap-1 flex-wrap"><div class="ReactionPopoverAnchor__B84pko"><button class="markdown-body" data-turbolinks="false"><div class="markdown-body safe-html-box__Uwc6Al"><p dir="auto">Why not disable telemetry by default for all installs, and then when a user in an interactive session does a <code class="notranslate">netlify init</code> or <code class="notranslate">netlify login</code>, just ask them for their consent that you send their data away?</p>
<p dir="auto">You could even do something like make it the default when a user hits enter:</p>
<p dir="auto"><code class="notranslate">transmit usage data to Netlify? [Y/n]: _</code></p>
<p dir="auto">Doing so silently and without any sort of notification or time window in which a user can cancel and not transmit is unethical and presumptuous, and, in my personal opinion, super rude.  A lack of consent withdrawal is <strong>not</strong> indication of affirmative consent.
